title: cutver
description: Which branches release, in which channel, for which ecosystem. Every key is optional; an absent file means cutver behaves as it always has.

$schema.description: This file, for editor completion. cutver ignores it.

schema.description: The config schema version — not the project's. A value above the one this cutver understands is refused rather than guessed at, because a newer schema may give a key a different meaning and the failure mode of guessing is an irreversible publish.

target.description: Which ecosystem this repository releases. Only needed when a repository has both a package.json and a Cargo.toml, where detection would otherwise have to guess. --adapter on the command line wins over this.

publish.description: Whether a tag publishes to the registry (npm, crates.io). What a tag *attaches* is `artifacts`. Omitted means the ecosystem default — true for node and bun, false for cargo, because publishing to crates.io reserves every workspace member name permanently and a Rust workspace is more often an application than a library. The pre-2.0 list form still parses and warns; it goes in 3.0.

changelog.description: Compile CHANGELOG.md from the commits. **cutver then owns the file and rewrites it whole on every release** — edits do not survive, and there is no `## [Unreleased]`. Each entry is a commit subject plus the first paragraph of its body. Omitted or `false` keeps the default: roll the `## [Unreleased]` heading and write no notes, because the version is mechanical and the prose is the work.

keep.description: Release sections kept in the file, newest first. `false` keeps every one. Defaults to 10 — a changelog that grows for the life of a project is the reason nobody scrolls to the bottom of one.

prompt.description: The instruction sent ahead of the notes, replacing the shipped one. Unlike the command, this belongs in the config: a prompt is data on a model’s stdin rather than something executed, and it is the part that needs tuning against a particular model. Only used when changelog.summarizer is on.

prereleases.description: Whether prereleases get their own heading. Off by default: a prerelease is a step toward a release rather than one, `latest` never pointed at it, and everything in it ships again under the stable version that follows. Excluding them widens the ranges rather than dropping the commits — a stable release measures from the previous stable tag, absorbing every prerelease between.

connector.description: Which request shape to use. `openai-compatible` covers OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Together, vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp and Ollama through `base_url`.

model.description: Passed through verbatim. cutver keeps no list of model names — it would be stale within the month.

base_url.description: Required for `openai-compatible`, where it is what names the provider; optional elsewhere. No default for the compatible connector on purpose — defaulting would send a repository’s notes somewhere it never named.

retry.description: Wait and try once more, for failures waiting can fix — a 429, a 5xx, a timeout. `true` waits one minute, the window rate limits are measured over; a number says how many minutes, up to 10. A wrong model name or a rejected key is never retried. Off by default.

with_body.description: Send whole commit bodies rather than the first paragraph of each. On by default — it is what lets one commit become several bullets.

summarizer.description: Where the GitHub release body goes to be rewritten. Writing it is the opt-in — there is no separate switch. `true` means the command in CUTVER_SUMMARIZE; a mapping names a provider. CHANGELOG.md is never summarised. There is deliberately no key for an API key: it is read from the environment, because this file is committed and published.

channels.description: Branch patterns keyed by what they produce. A channel not mentioned here keeps its default, so naming only `beta` does not switch `rc` off.

release.description: Branches that cut a stable release. Defaults to every branch; writing this list is the opt-in to strictness.

^[-_ ]*[A-Za-z]+([-_ ]+[A-Za-z]+)*[-_ ]*.description: Branches that cut a prerelease under this identifier. The key is the channel: it is the prerelease identifier in the version string and the dist-tag the release publishes under, so there is no separate tag field to drift out of step with it. camelCase, snake_case and spaces are normalised to kebab-case; digits are not accepted, because a counter that never matches its own pattern restarts at .0 on every run and the channel then reports 'nothing to release' forever.

folders.description: Directory globs. Each match is archived to <name>.tar.gz and attached as one asset. Relative to the repository root.

files.description: File globs. Each match is attached as its own asset, under its own name. Relative to the repository root.

artifacts.description: What a tag attaches to its release. `false` attaches nothing, `auto` finds the build output, or name the paths.

summarizer.description: **Pre-2.0.** The summariser goes under `changelog.summarizer:` now. This still parses and warns; it goes away in 3.0.

connector.description: Which request shape to use. `openai-compatible` covers OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Together, vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp and Ollama through `base_url`.

model.description: Passed through verbatim. cutver keeps no list of model names — it would be stale within the month.

base_url.description: Required for `openai-compatible`, where it is what names the provider; optional elsewhere. No default for the compatible connector on purpose — defaulting would send a repository’s notes somewhere it never named.

retry.description: Wait and try once more, for failures waiting can fix — a 429, a 5xx, a timeout. `true` waits one minute, the window rate limits are measured over; a number says how many minutes, up to 10. A wrong model name or a rejected key is never retried. Off by default.

branches.description: Literal names (`develop`), globs (`nightly/*`), or `{version}-<channel>` for a branch that declares its own base. A leading `release/` is stripped before matching.

sections.description: Section keys, in reading order. `breaking` collects the `!` and BREAKING CHANGE commits from every type and is listed first by default.
